title: Online order processing
prompt: Draw an activity diagram for processing an online order. The customer places an order and the system checks stock. If the item is in stock, payment is processed; if payment succeeds, the item is packed and shipped while a confirmation email is sent at the same time. If the item is out of stock or payment fails, the order is cancelled and the customer is notified.
checklist: One initial node and at least one final node
Actions for place order, check stock, process payment, pack, ship and send confirmation
A decision node for stock availability with labelled guards
A decision node for payment success with labelled guards
A fork and a join showing shipping and the confirmation email happening in parallel
A cancellation path that notifies the customer and reaches a final node
modelAnswer: Start, then Place order, then Check stock. A decision [in stock] leads to Process payment and [out of stock] leads to Cancel order. After payment, a second decision: [approved] leads to a fork whose two branches are Pack item then Ship item, and Send confirmation email; both meet at a join and then the final node. [declined] leads to Cancel order, then Notify customer, then the final node.
mermaid:
flowchart TD
  S((Start)) --> A[Place order]
  A --> B[Check stock]
  B --> D1{In stock?}
  D1 -- no --> X[Cancel order]
  D1 -- yes --> P[Process payment]
  P --> D2{Payment approved?}
  D2 -- no --> X
  D2 -- yes --> F[/Fork/]
  F --> K[Pack item]
  K --> H[Ship item]
  F --> E[Send confirmation email]
  H --> J[/Join/]
  E --> J
  X --> N[Notify customer]
  J --> Z(((End)))
  N --> Z

title: Library lending system
prompt: Draw a class diagram for a library. Members borrow copies of books. A book has a title, an author and an ISBN, and the library may own several copies of the same book. A loan records which member borrowed which copy, with a borrow date and a due date. Members are either students or staff, and staff may borrow for longer.
checklist: Classes for Member, Book, BookCopy (or Copy) and Loan
Attributes with sensible types, such as isbn, title, borrowDate and dueDate
At least one operation, such as borrow() or returnCopy()
A one-to-many association between Book and BookCopy with multiplicities
Loan associated with one Member and one BookCopy
Student and Staff shown as subclasses of Member using generalization
modelAnswer: Member (memberId, name; borrow(), returnCopy()) is the superclass of Student and Staff (hollow-triangle generalization). Book (isbn, title, author) 1 to 1..* BookCopy (copyId, status). Loan (borrowDate, dueDate, returnDate) is linked to exactly one Member and exactly one BookCopy; a Member has 0..* Loans and a BookCopy has 0..* Loans over time.
mermaid:
classDiagram
  class Member {
    +String memberId
    +String name
    +borrow(copy)
    +returnCopy(copy)
  }
  class Student
  class Staff
  class Book {
    +String isbn
    +String title
    +String author
  }
  class BookCopy {
    +String copyId
    +String status
  }
  class Loan {
    +Date borrowDate
    +Date dueDate
    +Date returnDate
  }
  Member <|-- Student
  Member <|-- Staff
  Book "1" --> "1..*" BookCopy : has
  Member "1" --> "0..*" Loan : makes
  BookCopy "1" --> "0..*" Loan : lent in

title: University enrolment
prompt: Draw an ER diagram for course enrolment. Students enrol in courses and receive a grade for each. Each course is taught by exactly one instructor, and an instructor can teach several courses. Each instructor belongs to one department. Include primary keys.
checklist: Entities for Student, Course, Instructor and Department
A primary key marked on every entity
A many-to-many relationship between Student and Course
The grade placed on the enrolment relationship (or an associative Enrolment entity), not on Student or Course
A one-to-many relationship from Instructor to Course
A one-to-many relationship from Department to Instructor
modelAnswer: Student (student_id PK, name) M:N Course (course_id PK, title, credits) through Enrolment, which carries the attribute grade. Instructor (instructor_id PK, name) 1:N Course. Department (department_id PK, name) 1:N Instructor. When converted to tables, Enrolment becomes a table whose key is (student_id, course_id).

title: User login
prompt: Draw a sequence diagram for logging in to a web application. The user submits a username and password in the browser. The browser sends them to the authentication server, which looks the user up in the database and verifies the password hash. On success a session token is returned and the dashboard is shown; on failure an error message is shown.
checklist: Lifelines for User, Browser, Authentication server and Database
Messages in time order from top to bottom
A request from the server to the database and a return message back
Return messages drawn as dashed lines
An alt fragment separating the success and failure outcomes
Activation bars on the lifelines while they are processing
modelAnswer: User to Browser: enter credentials. Browser to Auth server: login(username, password). Auth server to Database: findUser(username); Database returns the user record (dashed). Auth server verifies the hash (self-message). alt [valid]: Auth server returns a session token, Browser shows the dashboard. [invalid]: Auth server returns an error, Browser shows an error message.
mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  actor User
  participant Browser
  participant Auth as Authentication server
  participant DB as Database
  User->>Browser: Enter username and password
  Browser->>+Auth: login(username, password)
  Auth->>+DB: findUser(username)
  DB-->>-Auth: user record
  Auth->>Auth: verify password hash
  alt valid credentials
    Auth-->>Browser: session token
    Browser-->>User: show dashboard
  else invalid credentials
    Auth-->>-Browser: error
    Browser-->>User: show error message
  end

title: ATM
prompt: Draw a use case diagram for an ATM. A customer can withdraw cash, deposit cash, check the balance and transfer funds. Every one of these requires the customer to be authenticated first. A bank technician can refill cash and run maintenance. The bank's central system takes part in every transaction.
checklist: A system boundary labelled ATM
Actors for Customer, Technician and the Bank system placed outside the boundary
Use cases for withdraw, deposit, check balance and transfer
An Authenticate use case connected with «include» from the transaction use cases
Technician use cases for refilling cash and maintenance
Use cases named as verb phrases from the actor's point of view
modelAnswer: Inside the ATM boundary: Withdraw cash, Deposit cash, Check balance and Transfer funds, each with a dashed «include» arrow to Authenticate customer. Customer is associated with those four. Technician is associated with Refill cash and Perform maintenance. The Bank system is a secondary actor on the right, associated with the transaction use cases.
mermaid:
flowchart LR
  C([Customer])
  T([Technician])
  B([Bank system])
  subgraph ATM
    W(Withdraw cash)
    D(Deposit cash)
    K(Check balance)
    F(Transfer funds)
    A(Authenticate customer)
    R(Refill cash)
    M(Perform maintenance)
  end
  C --- W
  C --- D
  C --- K
  C --- F
  W -. include .-> A
  D -. include .-> A
  K -. include .-> A
  F -. include .-> A
  T --- R
  T --- M
  W --- B
  D --- B
  K --- B
  F --- B

title: Grade classification
prompt: Draw a flow chart that reads the scores of N students one at a time. For each score, it outputs Pass if the score is 60 or more and Fail otherwise. After all scores are read, it outputs the number of students who passed.
checklist: Start and end terminal symbols
Input/output symbols (parallelograms) for reading N and the scores and for printing
A loop with a decision that ends after N scores
A decision comparing the score with 60, with both branches labelled
A pass counter that is initialised before the loop and incremented on the Pass branch
Every arrow has a direction and every path reaches the end
modelAnswer: Start; read N; set count = 0 and i = 0. Decision i < N? If no: print count, End. If yes: read score; decision score >= 60? Yes: print Pass and add 1 to count. No: print Fail. Then add 1 to i and return to the loop decision.
mermaid:
flowchart TD
  S([Start]) --> I[/Read N/]
  I --> Z[count = 0, i = 0]
  Z --> L{i < N?}
  L -- no --> O[/Print count/]
  O --> E([End])
  L -- yes --> R[/Read score/]
  R --> D{score >= 60?}
  D -- yes --> P[/Print Pass/]
  P --> C[count = count + 1]
  D -- no --> F[/Print Fail/]
  C --> N[i = i + 1]
  F --> N
  N --> L
